newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS GRAB 2-1 SERIES LEAD WITH 6-3 WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS GRAB 2-1 SERIES LEAD WITH 6-3 WIN.

text.p: Eric Lindros scored a hat trick as the Philadelphia Flyers seized the lead in the NHL's Eastern Conference finals and regained momentum and home ice advantage with a 6-3 win over the New York Rangers on Tuesday.

The Flyers bounced back from Sunday's 5-3 loss in a big way, dominating the early play and responding to every challenge the Rangers mounted in the third period to take a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven series.

Rangers goaltender Mike Richter, who surrendered just four goals in the entire five-game series against New Jersey in the previous round, was beaten five times by the determined Flyers, failing to make amends for his teammates' defensive lapses.

"We could have used some big saves ... but they didn't come," said New York coach Colin Campbell, before adding, "It's too early to jump off the Mike Richter bandwagon. I think Mike will bounce back strong."
Petr Svoboda, Trent Klatt and Rod Brind'Amour scored the other goals for Philadelphia.

Russ Courtnall scored twice and Wayne Gretzky notched his 10th goal of the playoffs for New York as the Rangers twice tied the game in the third period only to see the Flyers quickly regain the lead each time.
"We came back and we could very easily have won that game," said Campbell. "We got a little sloppy ... you can't do that with the Flyers."
The Flyers opted to go with veteran goaltender Ron Hextall after Garth Snow allowed five goals on 10 shots in Game Two and the move paid off.
Hextall stopped all 16 shots he faced over the first two periods and finished with 25 saves.
"Hextall played a great game, I thought," said Flyers coach Terry Murray. "It was the kind of game I needed from him."

The Rangers, already undermanned with injuries to four forwards, were forced to play without regular defenceman Alexander Karpovtsev, who flew home to Russia after learning of the sudden death of his mother earlier Tuesday.
In addition, star defenceman Brian Leetch was struggling with a wrist injury. "You've seen Brian Leetch play for a long time, that was not Brian Leetch tonight," Campbell said.
Further adding to New York's manpower woes, replacement forward Ken Gernander left the game in the first minute with a concussion after being slammed into the boards by Klatt.
In contrast to Game Two, it was the Flyers who played with focus and fire.
Philadelphia jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the first period as Lindros opened the scoring at 7:33 on a wraparound.
Richter, diving back to cover the open side of his net, appeared to stop the shot. But a video replay showed he had swept the puck out of his net.
"I saw it cross the line. It went over by almost a foot," Lindros said.
At 12:03 Svoboda doubled the lead, blasting a slapshot though traffic and into the New York net after Richter had his dropped stick knocked away by one of the Flyers.
Philadelphia nearly made it 3-0 with about 5:40 left in the first, but a Paul Coffey slapper that fooled Richter slammed off the goalpost.
The Rangers turned up the pressure in the second period but they could not get through the huge Philadelphia defenders and the Flyers took a 2-0 lead into the third period.
That's when the Rangers came to life.
Just 43 seconds in, on a powerplay left over from the second period, Gretzky found Courtnall, who one-timed it past Hextall and the Rangers were on the board and the crowd was back into the game.
After a Philadelphia goal was disallowed because Brind'Amour was in the crease, Courtnall drove home a rebound of a Luc Robitaille shot to tie it 2-2 at 4:02 of the third.

But 2:33 later, John LeClair sent a perfect cross-ice pass to Lindros, who took two strides and fired the puck past Richter. "I got some great passes tonight. Johnny gave me a great pass," Lindros said.
Gretzky knotted the game again at 14:21 as Courtnall grabbed a loose puck behind the Flyers net and fed the Great One in front.
"They came back hard," said Hextall. "They can really turn it up and they certainly turned it up in the third period."
But the effort was nullified just 38 seconds later as Shjon Podein broke in on a 2-on-1, feeding Klatt, who blasted the puck past Richter.
Any suspense ended less than two minutes later when Brind'Amour found himself alone with the puck and centre ice and beat Richter on a breakaway.
Lindros ended the scoring and completed his hat trick with an empty netter in the final minute.
New York gets a chance to even the series Friday at home.
"They are a hell of a hockey club," said Lindros. "We have to be ready for whatever they do."
